pages: Tidewater Solar Cooperative - Annual Report 2025
Overview
Tidewater Solar Cooperative was founded in 2014 in Galway, Ireland.
At the end of 2025 the cooperative had 2,340 member households.
The board is chaired by Aoife Brennan, who was re-elected in April 2025.
Our mission is to give every member a share of locally generated solar power.
Generation
Installed capacity grew from 18.4 MW to 23.1 MW during 2025.
The cooperative produced 27.6 GWh of electricity in 2025.
The Ballyconneely array, rated at 6.2 MW, was commissioned in June 2025.
The average capacity factor across all sites was 13.6 percent.
Finances
Revenue was 4.82 million euro in 2025, up 11 percent from 4.34 million euro in 2024.
The net surplus for the year was 610,000 euro.
The cooperative returned 212,000 euro to members as dividends.
The board approved a dividend rate of 3.5 percent.
Operations
Tidewater employs 14 staff across three sites.
Inverter failures caused 9 days of downtime at the Clifden site in March 2025.
The 2 MWh battery storage pilot was delayed to 2026 because grid connection permits were not issued in time.
Outlook for 2026
The cooperative targets 30 MW of installed capacity by the end of 2026.
It plans to add 600 member households in 2026.
The board does not plan to raise member fees in 2026.
Grid curtailment rose to 7 percent of output in 2025 and is the main risk to revenue.
